cues.en: Mike: In this lecture I'm going to talk about underfitting and overfitting.
cues.zh: Mike：這堂談擬合不足與過度擬合。

cues.en: If I were an old school rapper, I would've called this lecture, "Mo' parameters, mo' problems."
cues.zh: 如果我是老派饒舌歌手，會把這堂叫作「參數愈多，問題愈多」。

cues.en: So let's see what overfitting and underfitting means.
cues.zh: 看看過度擬合與擬合不足是什麼意思。

cues.en: And there's like the kind of traditional classical ways that people think about overfitting and underfitting, but then I'm gonna talk about this kind of hidden,
cues.zh: 先談傳統、經典的理解方式，再談一種隱藏，

cues.en: yet dangerous form of overfitting that many people do not realize is taking place.
cues.zh: 卻危險的過度擬合，很多人沒有意識到它正在發生。

cues.en: Okay, so let's start with this dataset.
cues.zh: 從這份資料開始。

cues.en: Here we have some data X and Y.
cues.zh: 有 X 與 Y 資料。

cues.en: So it's just two variables and it's pretty clear visually that what's going on here is there's a trend in the data.
cues.zh: 只有兩個變數，視覺上很清楚，資料有一個趨勢。

cues.en: So there's some kind of like linear increase, and then it looks like there's also a bit of noise, or some kind of variability.
cues.zh: 有某種線性增加，另外似乎帶一點雜訊或變異。

cues.en: So here I fit the data with a 2-parameter model.
cues.zh: 用兩個參數的模型擬合。

cues.en: This was a polynomial regression, so you now know all about polynomial regressions, and it was a first order polynomial regression.
cues.zh: 這是多項式迴歸，你已經學過，是一階多項式迴歸。

cues.en: So we have an intercept and a linear term.
cues.zh: 有截距與線性項。

cues.en: So, you know, fits the data reasonably well.
cues.zh: 擬合得相當合理。

cues.en: Looks pretty plausible.
cues.zh: 看起來可信。

cues.en: So what I did here was fit the data with a 10-parameter model, and that's the orange plus signs.
cues.zh: 這裡用十個參數的模型擬合，是橘色加號。

cues.en: So there's 10 data points and 10 parameters in this model.
cues.zh: 10 個資料點，模型有 10 個參數。

cues.en: So you can see that the model fits the data perfectly, absolutely perfectly.
cues.zh: 可以看到，模型絕對完美地擬合。

cues.en: Zero noise, zero residuals. We fit every single data point.
cues.zh: 零雜訊、零殘差，每個資料點都擬合到。

cues.en: Now this is what's called overfitting, and I would like you to pause the video and think of why this is bad.
cues.zh: 這稱為過度擬合，請暫停，想想為什麼不好。

cues.en: You know, you might naively think that this is actually a good thing because we're fitting every data point perfectly.
cues.zh: 可能會天真地認為，每個資料點都完美擬合，應該很好。

cues.en: So I came up with three issues for why this is bad here.
cues.zh: 我想到三個問題。

cues.en: So pause the video, see if you can come up with three, at least three different reasons why overfitting is bad.
cues.zh: 暫停，看看能否想出至少三個過度擬合不好的理由。

cues.en: Okay? How did it go?
cues.zh: 結果如何？

cues.en: Did you come up with some?
cues.zh: 有想到嗎？

cues.en: So the first one that I identified is that it kind of violates like the spirit of statistics.
cues.zh: 第一，它有點違反統計學精神。

cues.en: You know, the goal of statistics is to fit data using models that are as simple as they can be, and only as complicated as they need to be.
cues.zh: 統計的目標，是模型盡可能簡單，只複雜到必要程度。

cues.en: And so I feel like this kind of violates the spirit of that statistical guideline.
cues.zh: 我覺得這違反那個指引的精神。

cues.en: This model seems overly complicated.
cues.zh: 模型似乎太複雜。

cues.en: A second problem is that we are going to be fitting a lot of noise.
cues.zh: 第二，會擬合大量雜訊。

cues.en: So I don't really know if, you know, the variability in these data points is meaningful, or if that's just random noise, maybe it's sampling variability.
cues.zh: 不知道這些資料點的變異是否有意義，或只是隨機雜訊，也許是抽樣變異。

cues.en: There's some individual differences.
cues.zh: 可能有個體差異。

cues.en: Maybe there's some other experimental factors that we're not controlling, or maybe there's just noise in the measurement technique.
cues.zh: 可能有沒控制的其他實驗因子，也可能是量測技術的雜訊。

cues.en: So I don't know if we really want to be capturing all of this noise.
cues.zh: 不知道是否真的想捕捉全部雜訊。

cues.en: This might be too sensitive to noise.
cues.zh: 這可能對雜訊太敏感。

cues.en: And the third problem, which I'm gonna highlight to you now, is generalizability.
cues.zh: 第三個問題，現在要強調的是泛化能力。

cues.en: Which of these two models, the 2-parameter model or the 10-parameter model, is likely to generalize to new data better?
cues.zh: 兩參數與十參數模型，哪個比較可能良好泛化到新資料？

cues.en: Well, to do that, I simulated this.
cues.zh: 為此進行模擬。

cues.en: So this is dataset one, and here I created dataset two.
cues.zh: 這是資料集一，再建立資料集二。

cues.en: And dataset two has the same linear relationship between X and Y, but a different set of random numbers built in.
cues.zh: 資料集二的 X 與 Y 有相同線性關係，但使用不同隨機數。

cues.en: So this, yeah, just the noise is a bit different.
cues.zh: 只是雜訊有些不同。

cues.en: So now you can see the 2-parameter model is also doing, you know, basically just as well in dataset two, as it is in dataset one.
cues.zh: 兩參數模型，在資料集二基本上仍與資料集一表現一樣好。

cues.en: But now the 10-parameter model is not doing very well.
cues.zh: 十參數模型卻表現不好。

cues.en: The predictions are kind of all over the place.
cues.zh: 預測到處亂跑。

cues.en: And the predictions, you know, if I just showed you this plot, you know, you wouldn't know which are the predictions and which are the real data.
cues.zh: 如果只給你這張圖，可能分不出哪些是預測，哪些是真實資料。

cues.en: They, you know, it looks like the model is not really able to generalize to new data sets.
cues.zh: 模型似乎無法泛化到新資料集。

cues.en: And that's kind of the whole point because in general, when we're doing statistics, we don't really care about this sample per se.
cues.zh: 這正是重點，因為一般做統計，不太關心這個特定樣本本身。

cues.en: What we care about is the population from which this sample was drawn.
cues.zh: 關心的是抽出樣本的母體。

cues.en: And so if we cannot generalize from this sample to even another sample, that really limits our confidence in the ability
cues.zh: 如果連另一個樣本都無法泛化，就會大幅限制我們對它

cues.en: to generalize from this sample to the entire population.
cues.zh: 從樣本泛化到整個母體的信心。

cues.en: Okay, so this is overfitting.
cues.zh: 這是過度擬合。

cues.en: Now let me show you underfitting, underfitting looks, something like this.
cues.zh: 現在示範擬合不足，像這樣。

cues.en: So we have a quadratic function in the data and then we're fitting it with a model that has two few parameters.
cues.zh: 資料有二次函數關係，但模型參數太少。

cues.en: So in fact, this model is failing to capture the complexity of the data.
cues.zh: 無法捕捉資料的複雜性。

cues.en: So this is underfitting.
cues.zh: 這就是擬合不足。

cues.en: We have too few parameters, we're not getting enough of the dynamics of the data.
cues.zh: 參數太少，沒有掌握足夠的資料動態。

cues.en: Overfitting means we have too many parameters and we are fitting too much of the data.
cues.zh: 過度擬合則是參數太多，擬合了太多資料。

cues.en: So neither one of these is really great, underfitting and overfitting.
cues.zh: 兩者都不好。

cues.en: Here's a brief summary.
cues.zh: 簡短整理。

cues.en: The red font highlights the bad things and the green font highlights the good things.
cues.zh: 紅字表示壞處，綠字表示好處。

cues.en: So overfitting, we are overly sensitive to noise.
cues.zh: 過度擬合，對雜訊太敏感。

cues.en: We're gonna be modeling more noise than signal.
cues.zh: 模型處理的雜訊會比訊號多。

cues.en: And underfitting is less sensitive to noise.
cues.zh: 擬合不足對雜訊較不敏感。

cues.en: It's more robust to noise in the data, so that's a good thing for underfitting.
cues.zh: 對資料雜訊更穩健，這是它的好處。

cues.en: So overfitting, there is one positive aspect of overfitting, which is that the model has increased sensitivity to small or subtle effects.
cues.zh: 過度擬合有個正面之處，模型對微小、細微效果更敏感。

cues.en: So if you have subtle effects in the data, then overfitting might help you identify those subtle effects.
cues.zh: 資料有細微效果時，它可能幫助辨識。

cues.en: Of course, this has to be balanced with noise because it's sometimes difficult to distinguish real subtle effects versus artifactual effects due to noise.
cues.zh: 當然必須與雜訊平衡，因為真實細微效果，與雜訊造成的假效果，有時很難區別。

cues.en: And with underfitting, you are less likely to detect true effects.
cues.zh: 擬合不足則較不容易偵測真正效果。

cues.en: That's like the example I showed in the previous slide where the linear model failed to capture the quadratic effect.
cues.zh: 例如上一張的線性模型，無法捕捉二次效果。

cues.en: Okay, overfitting has reduced generalizability, so does underfitting, and this you saw a few slides ago.
cues.zh: 過度擬合降低泛化能力，擬合不足也一樣，幾張之前看過。

cues.en: With overfitting you have a lot of parameters, so when you have more parameters, it becomes more and more difficult to estimate those parameters, particularly with limited data.
cues.zh: 過度擬合有很多參數，參數愈多，愈難估計，尤其資料有限。

cues.en: So over parameterized models can be less accurate, the parameters themselves can be harder to estimate.
cues.zh: 參數過多的模型可能較不準確，參數本身更難估計。

cues.en: Now underfitting has kind of the opposite pattern.
cues.zh: 擬合不足則相反。

cues.en: So we have fewer parameters for the amount of data, and that generally means that we're going to be able to have more confidence in the estimates of those parameters.
cues.zh: 相對資料量，參數較少，通常能對參數估計更有信心。

cues.en: And underfitting is also useful for a small amount of data.
cues.zh: 資料少時，擬合不足也有用途。

cues.en: If you only have a little bit of data, then it's better to have fewer parameters, rather than too many parameters.
cues.zh: 只有少量資料，參數少比太多好。

cues.en: Now to be clear, neither of these is good.
cues.zh: 但說清楚，兩者都不好。

cues.en: You know, I'm trying to be sort of journalistic, and point out that there are, you know, these aren't totally horrible, but obviously you wanna find the happy medium.
cues.zh: 我只是想客觀指出它們不全然糟糕，但顯然要找適中平衡。

cues.en: You wanna find the fitting that's less than overfitting, but more than underfitting.
cues.zh: 擬合程度，要低於過度擬合，又高於擬合不足。

cues.en: So picking between these two is kind of like, you know, the lesser of two evils here.
cues.zh: 在兩者間選，有點像兩害取其輕。

cues.en: So how do you know the correct number of parameters?
cues.zh: 如何知道正確參數數量？

cues.en: How do you make sure that your model is sufficiently complex that you're not underfitting the data, but also sufficiently simple that you're not overfitting the data?
cues.zh: 如何確保模型夠複雜，不會擬合不足，又夠簡單，不會過度擬合？

cues.en: So basically you have to use a combination of intuition, critical thinking, and formal model comparisons.
cues.zh: 基本上，結合直覺、批判性思考與正式模型比較。

cues.en: If you're working with a small number of dimensions in your data, then you can just visualize the data and make an informed decision.
cues.zh: 資料維度少時，可以視覺化，做有根據的判斷。

cues.en: So that's like all the examples that I showed so far in this video were with two dimensional data sets.
cues.zh: 就像這支影片目前的例子，都是二維資料集。

cues.en: So in that case, we could just look at the data and make a reasonable guess.
cues.zh: 看資料，就能合理猜測。

cues.en: So, but when you start to have larger data sets and more complex experiments, then you're gonna need formal model comparisons.
cues.zh: 資料集更大、實驗更複雜，就需要正式模型比較。

cues.en: Now, I've already introduced you to this idea with the discussion of polynomial regression.
cues.zh: 多項式迴歸已介紹過這個概念。

cues.en: So that was with using the Bayes Information Criterion in order to determine, to quantify the relationship between model complexity and model fit.
cues.zh: 透過貝氏資訊準則，量化模型複雜度與擬合程度的關係。

cues.en: So that's already one way to know the correct number of parameters for a model.
cues.zh: 這是找出正確參數數量的一種方式。

cues.en: In the, it's actually not the next lecture, it's in two lectures from now, I'm gonna show you another method.
cues.zh: 不是下一堂，而是再過兩堂，會展示另一個方法。

cues.en: It's a method for formally comparing.
cues.zh: 正式比較，

cues.en: So statistically mathematically comparing different models that are similar to each other, but vary in the number of parameters.
cues.zh: 以統計、數學方法比較相似，但參數數量不同的模型。

cues.en: They vary in their complexity.
cues.zh: 也就是複雜度不同。

cues.en: But as I mentioned, you also need to just use a little bit of critical thinking and careful thought to avoid overfitting and underfitting.
cues.zh: 但如前所述，也需要批判性思考與謹慎判斷，避免兩種問題。

cues.en: Okay, so this, everything I've discussed so far is kind of like the traditional classical textbook version of overfitting data.
cues.zh: 目前討論的，都是傳統經典教科書版本的過度擬合。

cues.en: There's actually another way of overfitting data, and that's often called "Researcher degrees of freedom."
cues.zh: 其實還有一種，常稱為「研究者自由度」。

cues.en: It's also sometimes called hidden overfitting.
cues.zh: 有時叫隱藏過度擬合。

cues.en: And this is overfitting that people do because they want to do good analyses and they're unsure about exactly which analyses are appropriate for their data.
cues.zh: 因為想做好分析，卻不確定哪種分析適合資料，而造成過度擬合。

cues.en: So "Researcher degrees of freedom" is basically the idea that you, the researcher, the statistician, the data analyst, you have many choices for how to clean the data,
cues.zh: 研究者自由度，是指研究者、統計學家、資料分析師，有許多資料清理，

cues.en: organize the data, filter the data, select data, and you also have choices for which statistical models to run, how many models to run, how to parameterize those models.
cues.zh: 整理、篩選、選取的選擇，也能選統計模型、模型數量，以及參數化方式。

cues.en: So there's all sorts of choices, conscious choices that you can make.
cues.zh: 各種可以刻意做的選擇。

cues.en: And each time you make a choice, you're actually testing a new model of the data.
cues.zh: 每次選擇，其實都是在測試新的資料模型。

cues.en: So let me give you an example.
cues.zh: 舉個例子。

cues.en: Let's say you have a data set and you have three different statistical models that you're comparing.
cues.zh: 有一份資料集，要比較三種統計模型。

cues.en: So you test models A, B, and C on the same data, and now your heart is in the right place, you want to do the right thing, you want to model the data in a good way.
cues.zh: 在同一份資料測試 A、B、C，出發點良好，想做正確的事、好好建模。

cues.en: And you don't know a priori, which of these models is really the right way to model the data.
cues.zh: 事先不知道哪個才是正確方式。

cues.en: You don't know which approach is optimal.
cues.zh: 不知道哪種最佳。

cues.en: So of course you're gonna test three, that seems like a good thing to do.
cues.zh: 所以測三個，似乎是好事。

cues.en: So, but then you look at the results and you're like, you know, I'm not so happy with how I clean these data.
cues.zh: 但看結果後，覺得資料清理得不太滿意。

cues.en: So you go back to the raw dataset and you clean the data more, you filter the data in a different way, you use different criteria to clean the data,
cues.zh: 回到原始資料，進一步清理、用不同方式篩選、不同標準清理，

cues.en: and then you test these three models again.
cues.zh: 再測三個模型。

cues.en: And then it turns out that model B with the re-cleaned data gives really good results using an alpha threshold of 0.05.
cues.zh: 重新清理後，B 模型在 alpha 門檻 0.05，得到很好的結果。

cues.en: Now, I would like you to pause the video and think for a little bit about what is, first of all, what is the problem here?
cues.zh: 請暫停想想，首先，這有什麼問題？

cues.en: And/or, you know, maybe you think there isn't a problem, but clearly I think there's a problem, otherwise I wouldn't have gone into this.
cues.zh: 也許覺得沒問題，但顯然我認為有，否則不會談。

cues.en: So what is the issue here?
cues.zh: 問題是什麼？

cues.en: Why do we have "Researcher degrees of freedom?"
cues.zh: 為什麼有研究者自由度？

cues.en: And in particular, I would like you to think about what is the actual P threshold.
cues.zh: 尤其希望你思考，實際 P 門檻是多少。

cues.en: So I said that we use an alpha threshold of 0.05, a statistical significance threshold of 0.05, but what is the actual P threshold here?
cues.zh: 說是 alpha 0.05、統計顯著門檻 0.05，但實際 P 門檻是多少？

cues.en: Okay, pause the video.
cues.zh: 暫停。

cues.en: All right, how did it go?
cues.zh: 結果如何？

cues.en: Did you think of some reasons?
cues.zh: 想到理由了嗎？

cues.en: So the actual P threshold is difficult to compute exactly without knowing more information, but it's certainly gonna be larger than 0.05,
cues.zh: 沒有更多資訊，很難精確計算，但肯定大於 0.05，

cues.en: and the upper bound is 0.3.
cues.zh: 上界是 0.3。

cues.en: So let me explain how I got this number, 0.3.
cues.zh: 解釋 0.3 怎麼來。

cues.en: So we're actually doing six tests each evaluated at 0.05.
cues.zh: 其實做了六次檢定，每次都以 0.05 評估。

cues.en: So we do models A, B, and C, that's three tests, and then we clean the data twice.
cues.zh: A、B、C 三個模型，加上兩次資料清理。

cues.en: So that gives us a total of six tests, and each test is evaluated at 0.05.
cues.zh: 總共六次檢定，每次 0.05。

cues.en: Now, the reason why the alpha threshold is actually gonna be less than 0.3 is because these six tests are not actually independent of each other.
cues.zh: 實際 alpha 門檻小於 0.3，是因為六次檢定並不彼此獨立。

cues.en: There are some dependencies that's built into this testing and that's because we're working with the same data and probably these models are all sort of related to each other.
cues.zh: 使用同一份資料，而且模型大概也相關，所以檢定內建一些相依性。

cues.en: Okay? So we don't know exactly what the alpha threshold is, but it's certainly larger than 0.05.
cues.zh: 不知道確切 alpha 門檻，但肯定大於 0.05。

cues.en: So this is what's known as, "Researcher degrees of freedom," or overfitting.
cues.zh: 這就是研究者自由度，或過度擬合。

cues.en: The issue here again comes back to overfitting noise and lack of generalizability or reduced generalizability.
cues.zh: 問題同樣是過度擬合雜訊，以及缺乏、降低泛化能力。

cues.en: So it could be that model B with this, you know, specific criteria for cleaning the data.
cues.zh: B 模型加這套特定清理標準，

cues.en: That really does work best in this particular sample.
cues.zh: 確實可能最適合這個特定樣本。

cues.en: But then when we go to a different sample, we might find that model B actually fits the data really poorly.
cues.zh: 但換另一個樣本，可能 B 擬合很差。

cues.en: And maybe that's because model B was just overly complicated and fitting noise in the original data.
cues.zh: 也許 B 太複雜，只是在擬合原始資料的雜訊。

cues.en: So this is a pretty insidious problem.
cues.zh: 這是相當隱晦的問題。

cues.en: How do you avoid researcher overfitting?
cues.zh: 如何避免研究者過度擬合？

cues.en: So there's a few ways, although again, the conclusion is gonna be, you know, you have to be mindful of this issue.
cues.zh: 有幾種方式，但結論仍是必須留意。

cues.en: You have to be a good scientist and think critically.
cues.zh: 當個好的科學家，批判性思考。

cues.en: So you have to, so one strategy is to decide your complete analysis pipeline in advance.
cues.zh: 一種策略，是事先決定完整分析流程。

cues.en: So before you even look at the data, you write down somewhere, you make a commitment to say, this is how I'm gonna clean the data.
cues.zh: 甚至看資料前，就寫下承諾，說明將如何清理，

cues.en: This is how I'm gonna sort the data.
cues.zh: 如何排序，

cues.en: This is how I'm gonna filter the data, and this is exactly what analysis I'm gonna run.
cues.zh: 如何篩選，以及確切執行哪個分析。

cues.en: These are the parameters that I'm gonna use.
cues.zh: 會用哪些參數。

cues.en: This is how I'll set up the model.
cues.zh: 如何設定模型。

cues.en: This is gonna be my statistical threshold, and so on.
cues.zh: 統計門檻等等。

cues.en: So every analysis that you're going to run, you specify in advance.
cues.zh: 所有分析事先指定。

cues.en: This is kind of like a pre-registered report in science, where, you know, you write the research paper before you actually collect the data.
cues.zh: 有點像科學中的預先註冊報告，收集資料之前先寫研究論文。

cues.en: So, and then the idea is that anytime you deviate from your plan, you're allowed to deviate from your plan, but you have to state that clearly.
cues.zh: 可以偏離計畫，但每次偏離，都必須清楚說明。

cues.en: So then other people can evaluate whether they think that your deviation is likely to generalize to new data sets.
cues.zh: 其他人才能評估，這種偏離是否可能泛化到新資料。

cues.en: Okay? So this is one method.
cues.zh: 這是一種方式。

cues.en: Another method would be that you know in advance that you want to do some exploration, you wanna do some model exploration, you test different statistical models
cues.zh: 另一種，是事先知道想做探索、嘗試不同統計模型，

cues.en: and different model complexities, play around with different ways of filtering and cleaning the data.
cues.zh: 不同複雜度，以及不同資料篩選、清理方式。

cues.en: So that part's fine.
cues.zh: 這沒問題。

cues.en: You say that that's gonna be an exploratory or development phase, but then you only work through that development, that exploration on a sample of data.
cues.zh: 說明是探索或開發階段，但只在一部分資料上進行。

cues.en: So you just take a little bit of your data, maybe it's 10% of your data or 5% of your data depending on how much data you have.
cues.zh: 取少量資料，依總資料量，可能取 10% 或 5%。

cues.en: And then you, you know, you employ "Researcher degrees of freedom" on that sample of the data and then that allows you to customize an analysis pipeline.
cues.zh: 在那部分資料運用研究者自由度，訂製分析流程。

cues.en: And then once you have that analysis pipeline, you apply that pipeline to the rest of the data.
cues.zh: 流程確定後，套用到其餘資料。

cues.en: Now this is actually just like a training testing set from cross validation.
cues.zh: 其實就像交叉驗證中的訓練與測試集。

cues.en: It's just, you know, this is a little bit more informal because you're doing this as a researcher, not as an algorithm, but this is also a good way.
cues.zh: 只是比較非正式，由研究者做，而不是演算法，但也是好方法。

cues.en: And I have to say, this is the way that I have always done it in my, you know, 20 years, or whatever, of data analysis.
cues.zh: 我必須說，自己二十年左右的資料分析，一直這樣做。

cues.en: I will customize an analysis and data cleaning pipeline in one dataset and then I will apply that same pipeline blindly
cues.zh: 在一份資料集訂製分析與清理流程，再把相同流程盲目套用，

cues.en: without, you know, hopefully without any deviations to the other 20 or 30 or 50 datasets that I have in this experiment.
cues.zh: 希望完全不偏離，到實驗中另外 20、30 或 50 份資料集。

cues.en: Okay, so in this 50 Cents lecture you learned about overfitting and underfitting why they are bad, but also why they can be good.
cues.zh: 這堂向 50 Cent 致敬的課，學到過度擬合與擬合不足，為什麼不好，也為什麼可能有好處。

cues.en: I think it's important to also appreciate that overfitting and underfitting can have positive aspects.
cues.zh: 我認為，了解它們的正面之處也重要。

cues.en: If you have a small data set, it might be good to lean on the side of underfitting because you can be more confident about the parameters that you're estimating with a small amount of data.
cues.zh: 資料少時，偏向擬合不足可能較好，因為能對少量資料所估計的參數更有信心。

cues.en: Nonetheless, the goal, of course, is to find the happy medium, somewhere between overfitting and underfitting.
cues.zh: 但目標當然仍是找到兩者之間的適中平衡。
